posts.title: CTU promotes lifelong learning through Systemwide Campus Book Fair 2026
posts.excerpt: Strengthening access to learning resources and supporting lifelong learning, Cebu Technological University-Main Campus hosted the Systemwide Campus Book Fair 2026 on November 4-5 at the Library and Resource Cen…
posts.contentHtml:
Strengthening access to learning resources and supporting lifelong learning, Cebu Technological University-Main Campus hosted the Systemwide Campus Book Fair 2026 on November 4-5 at the Library and Resource Center, bringing together publishers, educators, and learners in a two-day celebration of books and knowledge.

With the theme “Basa, Salin, Daloy: Empowering Minds Through Books, Innovation and Lifelong Learning,” the event brought together publishers, educators, and learners to foster a culture of reading, knowledge exchange, and lifelong learning through greater access to educational resources.

University Head Librarian Ms. Morena E. Carlos led the book fair, which featured curated book selections and recommendations from faculty members and library personnel. Participants reviewed available publications and identified learning resources that could support academic programs, instruction, and library collection development.

The event featured an OBSCI pitching session led by Dr. Ronald M. Galindo, former Dean of the College of Engineering, who highlighted the concepts Recover, Share, Design, Utilize, and Impact. His presentation emphasized the value of preserving knowledge, sharing resources, developing ideas, and transforming them into meaningful contributions.

A presentation by a representative from Linar Libri introduced digital library platforms and online resources (websites) designed to improve access to research and educational materials for students, faculty, and researchers.

The demonstration highlighted the role of digital library platforms in supporting teaching, research, and lifelong learning through improved access to academic resources and information.

Through the initiative, CTU reinforced the value of both printed and digital learning resources in supporting academic development, encouraging reading, and providing accessible opportunities for continuous learning./Zandel Kim S. Ebro, BSFIL Intern.
posts.author: Junas Flores

posts.title: ACCREDITATION UPDATE | CTU Main, Carmen Campuses advance quality standards with AACCUP Accreditation Survey
posts.excerpt: To strengthen the quality of its academic programs and institutional services, Cebu Technological University (CTU) underwent a three-day accreditation survey visit by the Accrediting Agency of Chartered College…
posts.contentHtml:
To strengthen the quality of its academic programs and institutional services, Cebu Technological University (CTU) underwent a three-day accreditation survey visit by the Accrediting Agency of Chartered Colleges and Universities in the Philippines (AACCUP) from November 11 to 13 at its Main and Carmen campuses.

Programs evaluated included:

CTU Main Campus

Level IV Phase 2 Revisit All Areas

Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering

Bachelor of Science in Industrial Engineering

Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering

Bachelor Science in Mechanical Engineering

Level III Phase 2

Bachelor of Science in Tourism Management

CTU Carmen Campus

Level III Phase 2

Master of Arts in Education major in Administrtation and Supervision

Bachelor of Secondary Education major in Mathematics

The AACCUP survey team was led by Dr. Geraldin B. Dela Cruz of Tarlac Agricultural University (TAU), Overall Coordinator for Main Campus (Cluster I), alongside Dr. Job D. Paguio of Bataan Peninsula State University (BPSU), Overall Coordinator for Carmen and Main Campuses (Cluster II). 

Key institutional areas assessed during the survey included research, extension, library services, faculty development, graduate performance, licensure examination results, community service, international linkages, and planning processes.

The five-day survey visit was facilitated by the Quality Assurance Office under University Director Dr. Meralei J. Lawas, with support from Campus QA Chairs Engr. Ike A. Baguio (Main), Dr. Kafferine D. Yamagishi (Main), and Dr. Bonifacio M. Amper, Jr. (Carmen).

Present during the survey visit were Main Campus Director Dr. Gregorion P. Pajaron Jr.; Carmen Campus Director Dr. Anthony S. Ilano; Dr. Joecyn N. Archival, Dean of the College of Engineering; and Dr. Amelia Girly L. Aranas, Dean of the College of Management and Entrepreneurship.

The survey visit affirms CTU’s commitment to institutional excellence and continuous quality enhancement, supporting its pursuit of nationally and globally recognized standards in higher education.

posts.title: Sidhi Performing Arts showcases CTU culture and talent across October events
posts.excerpt: Cebu Technological University’s (CTU) Sidhi Performing Arts maintained an active presence in academic, government, and community events throughout October 2026, showcasing Filipino culture and student talent wh…
posts.contentHtml:
Cebu Technological University’s (CTU) Sidhi Performing Arts maintained an active presence in academic, government, and community events throughout October 2026, showcasing Filipino culture and student talent while supporting key institutional and public engagements.

The group opened the month with performances at the 37th National Statistics Month Opening Ceremony on October 1, the Higher Education Partnership Conference 2026 on October 2, and the 3rd Trimester General Orientation on October 3.

On October 5, Sidhi performed during the RDC Week Culmination and the World Teachers’ Day Celebration, recognizing regional development efforts and honoring educators. They further joined the Mental Health Week Walk 2026 and the 37th National Statistics Month Campus Leg on October 13, promoting student well-being and statistical awareness.

Sidhi capped off its October engagements on October 29 with performances at the 29th CTU Local Job Fair and the 37th National Statistics Month Closing Ceremony, earning certificates of recognition for its contributions to both events.

Through Sidhi Performing Arts, the University promotes the preservation of cultural heritage, develops students’ artistic talents, and strengthens community engagement while fostering pride in Filipino identity.

posts.title: ACCREDITATION UPDATE | CTU Barili, Carmen, and San Francisco Campuses secure Level III Re-accreditation for three programs
posts.excerpt: In pursuit of academic excellence and continuous quality improvement, Cebu Technological University secures Level III Re-accredited status for three programs across its Barili, Carmen, and San Francisco campuse…
posts.contentHtml:
In pursuit of academic excellence and continuous quality improvement, Cebu Technological University secures Level III Re-accredited status for three programs across its Barili, Carmen, and San Francisco campuses from the Accrediting Agency of Chartered Colleges and Universities in the Philippines (AACCUP), Inc.

According to the AACCUP accreditation results, the programs met all mandatory compliance requirements and were granted Level III Re-accredited status, valid from September 1, 2026, to August 31, 2030. The programs are as follows:

CTU Barili Campus
Master of Science in Crop Science (Level III Re-accredited)

Carmen Campus
Bachelor of Science in Hospitality Management (Level III Re-accredited)

San Francisco Campus
Master of Arts in Education, major in Administration and Supervision (Level III Re-accredited)

The accreditation outcomes affirm the University’s ongoing efforts to maintain high academic standards, strengthen curricular offerings, and ensure compliance with quality-assurance measures prescribed by national accrediting bodies.
posts.author: Junas Flores

posts.title: Indonesians advance engineering strides with CTU
posts.excerpt: University of Lambung Mangkurat (ULM) recently engaged with CTU to calibrate engineering projects, following the agreement sealed early this year. The onsite visit proved both institutions’ focus on concretizin…
posts.contentHtml:
University of Lambung Mangkurat (ULM) recently engaged with CTU to calibrate engineering projects, following the agreement sealed early this year.

The onsite visit proved both institutions’ focus on concretizing platforms augmenting Southeast Asia’s engineering initiatives.

Based in Kalimantan, ULM brings a research perspective to the partnership through its disciplines, including civil, chemical, environmental, mechanical, mining, geological, and electrical engineering.

Both institutions expressed keen interest in pursuing joint research funding opportunities and improving laboratory facilities to support the future collaborative tasks.

Initiated by CTU Main academic Dr. Hana Astrid Tunacao, the alliance sees multiple ventures that would bring Cebu and Kalimantan much closer./ IAI

posts.title: Indonesia’s top HEI learns ‘talking global’ from Tuburan expert
posts.excerpt: Institut Teknologi Sepuluh Nopember’s Creabiz International Week in October included Dr. Angen May Charcos’ master class on global discourse. Participants in Surabaya heard CTU Tuburan academic dissecting cultu…
posts.contentHtml:
Institut Teknologi Sepuluh Nopember’s Creabiz International Week in October included Dr. Angen May Charcos’ master class on global discourse.

Participants in Surabaya heard CTU Tuburan academic dissecting cultural identity, representation, and stereotypes in media. She also addressed misinformation, trust, and the fight for credible information in the age of algorithms and AI.

Dr. Charcos, originally intending to present her ideas onsite, pursued her commitment online . Layered onto her talk were mobility experiences from students Keign Amor Ramirez and Nikka Formoso.

CTU and the Indonesian HEI has had multiple cooperative frameworks to date./IAI

posts.title: CTU-CCMC-College of Nursing honored as Top 1 Performing Nursing School
posts.excerpt: Cebu Technological University–Cebu City Medical Center (CTU-CCMC) College of Nursing has been recognized as the country’s No. 1 performing nursing school in the 50–99 examinees category following its outstandin…
posts.contentHtml:
Cebu Technological University–Cebu City Medical Center (CTU-CCMC) College of Nursing has been recognized as the country’s No. 1 performing nursing school in the 50–99 examinees category following its outstanding performance in the August–September 2026 Philippine Nurse Licensure Examination (PNLE).

The university received the national recognition during the Oath-Taking Ceremony for New Professional Nurses yesterday at the Cebu Doctors’ University Auditorium in Mandaue City.

The ceremony gathered newly licensed nurses, academic leaders, and representatives of the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) and the Board of Nursing to welcome the newest members of the nursing profession.

Accepting the recognition on behalf of the university were CTU OIC-President Dr. Jonita V. Literatus and CTU-CCMC College of Nursing Assistant Dean for Administration Mrs. Divine Grace M. Cortes.

The distinction highlights the College of Nursing’s consistent record of academic excellence, with the Class of 2026 achieving a 100% passing rate in the PNLE for the fifth consecutive year.

This sustained performance reflects the institution’s commitment to producing competent, highly qualified, and board-ready nursing professionals.

CTU-CCMC College of Nursing also emerged as the only nursing school in Cebu to earn the Top 1 distinction in its examinee category, further strengthening the university’s standing in nursing education.

Adding to this achievement, CTU-CCMC alumna Vianca Abegail T. Guarin, RN, earned a place among the country’s topnotchers, ranking tenth nationwide with a board rating of 90.40%.

These accomplishments underscore the university’s continued pursuit of excellence in nursing education and its commitment to developing healthcare professionals equipped to serve communities and contribute to the advancement of the healthcare sector.

More than a testament to exceptional board examination performance, this recognition affirms CTU-CCMC College of Nursing’s position as a leading institution in nursing education and inspires future generations of nurses to uphold the same standard of excellence.
posts.author: Junas Flores

posts.title: CTU celebrates 17th Charter Anniversary with service, sports, and culture
posts.excerpt: Commemorating 17 years since its conversion into a university through Republic Act No. 9744 on November 10, 2009, Cebu Technological University (CTU) honored its Charter Anniversary celebration today with activ…
posts.contentHtml:
Commemorating 17 years since its conversion into a university through Republic Act No. 9744 on November 10, 2009, Cebu Technological University (CTU) honored its Charter Anniversary celebration today with activities highlighting service, unity, and excellence.

Morning sessions featured the oath-taking ceremony of newly hired and promoted university personnel, while the afternoon was marked by the continuation of the sports tournament and Larong Pinoy competitions.

Evening festivities featured live band entertainment, cultural performances, and special awards recognizing excellence in Zumba, sports, and campus support.

The celebration concluded with a solidarity dance led by OIC-University President Dr. Jonita V. Literatus, together with fellow university officials, and joined by employees and students from CTU campuses across the province, symbolizing the University’s unity and commitment to advancing its mission and vision in the years ahead.

posts.title: CTU silver-sponsors ALL ASIA 2027 rankings launch
posts.excerpt: Institutions across Asia await the launch of AppliedEdu ALL ASIA 2027 rankings on November 30th at the AppliedHE Xchange online event, with CTU as one of its silver sponsors. CTU will soon know its place in Asi…
posts.contentHtml:
Institutions across Asia await the launch of AppliedEdu ALL ASIA 2027 rankings on November 30th at the AppliedHE Xchange online event, with CTU as one of its silver sponsors.

CTU will soon know its place in Asia [for the first time using the AppliedHE metrics], following the release of the ASEAN 2027 rankings last month by the same company [formerly AppliedHE] known for its separate assessment of public and private colleges and universities.

Layered onto the launch will be key dialogs with policymakers, academics, researchers and leaders, that would touch on narratives within the academia-industry crossroads.

Highlighted is the grand panel moderated by CTU Internationalization and ASEAN Integration Director Dr. Rhodora Magan. She will be joined by speakers from renowned institutions in Asia.

Other sponsors are top-tier HEIs including The Hang Seng University of Hong Kong, and Malaysia’s Asia Pacific University of Technology and Innovation and Sunway University./IAI Office

posts.title: 113 CTU employees take Oath of Office, strengthening University workforce
posts.excerpt: As part of Cebu Technological University’s 17th Charter Anniversary, 113 newly hired and promoted personnel from across the University’s campuses formally took their oath of office today at the CebuTech Gymnasi…
posts.contentHtml:
As part of Cebu Technological University’s 17th Charter Anniversary, 113 newly hired and promoted personnel from across the University’s campuses formally took their oath of office today at the CebuTech Gymnasium, Main Campus.

The oathtaking ceremony, administered by OIC-University President Dr. Jonita V. Literatus, marked the official assumption of duties of employees appointed and promoted for Calendar Years 2025-2026.

Among those sworn in were 88 newly hired personnel, comprising 28 faculty members and 60 non-teaching staff, alongside 25 promoted employees, including one faculty member and 24 non-teaching personnel.

Joining the ceremony were Dr. Ramel C. Genobiagon, Vice President for Administration and Finance; Dr. Reylan G. Capuno, Vice President for Academic Affairs; and Dr. Rosein A. Ancheta Jr. Vice President for PERG, as well as CTU Main Campus Director Dr. Gregorio P. Pajaron Jr., and Supervising Administrative Officer (HRMO IV) Dr. Jana Gloria F. Almerino.

The appointments and promotions reinforce CTU’s efforts to build a competent workforce and strengthen public service delivery across the University.

posts.title: CTU kicks off 17th University Anniversary, honoring a legacy of excellence and growth
posts.excerpt: Marking 17 years of transformative growth as a university, Cebu Technological University (CTU) officially opened its University Anniversary festivities today, bringing together campuses across the province unde…
posts.contentHtml:
Marking 17 years of transformative growth as a university, Cebu Technological University (CTU) officially opened its University Anniversary festivities today, bringing together campuses across the province under the theme, “Seventeen Years, One Heartbeat: Honoring Our Heritage, Shaping CTU’s Future with Purpose and Excellence.”

This year’s celebration commemorates 17 years since CTU attained University status on November 10, 2009, through Republic Act No. 9744, which was signed into law by former President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo.

The milestone highlights the institution’s transformation from the Cebu Trade School to one of the country’s leading state universities.

OIC-University President Dr. Jonita V. Literatus joined the opening program and led the ribbon-cutting ceremony for the anniversary booths and product displays.

The festivities began with a flag-raising ceremony and a grand parade, joined by students and employees, followed by the opening of exhibit booths and product displays, and a solidarity meeting of athletes.

Afternoon activities featured Larong Pinoy and sports tournaments in badminton, pickleball, lawn tennis, basketball, and volleyball, fostering camaraderie, wellness, and sportsmanship among participants.

As CTU celebrates 17 years as a University, the gathering highlighted the institution’s continuing pursuit of academic excellence, innovation, and public service that uplift communities and transform lives.
posts.author: Junas Flores

posts.title: Playground demonstration and fireworks highlight Angara Sports Fest 2026 Opening
posts.excerpt: First and second year students of Cebu Technological University – Carmen Campus, through their PATHFIT classes, performed a playground demonstration during the opening of the Angara Sports Fest 2026 yesterday a…
posts.contentHtml:
First and second year students of Cebu Technological University – Carmen Campus, through their PATHFIT classes, performed a playground demonstration during the opening of the Angara Sports Fest 2026 yesterday at the Carmen Oval Plaza led by Sinamayan Dance Troupe.

The demonstration featured synchronized routines that showcased the students’ discipline, coordination, and teamwork as part of their PATHFIT performance. Their presentation drew cheers and applause from delegates, faculty, and spectators who gathered for the opening program.

All the hard work, sacrifices, and long hours of practice under the heat of the sun paid off as the field demonstration became a colorful and unforgettable experience in commemorating the Angara Sports Fest.

The evening concluded with a dazzling fireworks display that lit up the plaza, bringing students together as one CTU community and formally marking the start of the week-long sports celebration.

Moreover, the opening ceremony aimed to formally welcome and recognize all the delegates from various CTU campuses./Kierex Colipano

posts.title: 5th Angara Unity Cup 2026 opens with Grand Parade, Torch Lighting, and Candidate Presentation
posts.excerpt: The 5th Angara Unity Cup 2026 officially opened today, November 8, with a vibrant parade from Cebu Technological University (CTU) Carmen Campus to the Carmen Plaza Grandstand, followed by the ceremonial lightin…
posts.contentHtml:
The 5th Angara Unity Cup 2026 officially opened today, November 8, with a vibrant parade from Cebu Technological University (CTU) Carmen Campus to the Carmen Plaza Grandstand, followed by the ceremonial lighting of the Olympic flame and the presentation of the Mr. and Ms. CebuTech candidates.

Delegates from 16 CTU campuses joined the parade, including athletes, university officials, tournament managers, and their respective pageant representatives.

The parade was welcomed by community supporters and enlivened by Sinamayan through cultural dances and musical performances representing the participating campuses.

A highlight of the opening ceremony was the ceremonial torch lighting led by University President Dr. Jonita V. Literatus and CTU Carmen Campus Director Dr. Anthony D. Ilano. Arnis SCUAA players Jannalyn Ycoy and Clint Jhon Cañete served as torchbearers, symbolizing unity, sportsmanship, and the spirit of competition.

Meanwhile, the Mr. and Ms. CebuTech candidates took center stage as they were formally introduced to the audience, representing their respective campuses in the much-anticipated pageant competition.

The opening festivities mark the beginning of a week-long celebration of athletic excellence, camaraderie, and unity among the CTU campuses./Kheven C. Aguanta, Aegen L. Taneo & Cherry Mae B. Andrada

Photos: Kristelyn Talabok, Ashley Nicole Arenza & and Kristelyn Talabok | Layout: Stephanie V. Jayson

posts.title: CTU Carmen welcomes delegates for the 5th ANGGARA UNITY CUP 2026
posts.excerpt: Cebu Technological University (CTU) – Carmen Campus officially welcomed delegates today, November 8, for the 5th Anggara Unity Cup 2026, an annual university-wide sports gathering that brings together student-a…
posts.contentHtml:
Cebu Technological University (CTU) – Carmen Campus officially welcomed delegates today, November 8, for the 5th Anggara Unity Cup 2026, an annual university-wide sports gathering that brings together student-athletes from different CTU campuses.

The sports event gathers athletes from CTU Main Campus, Barili, Pinamungajan, Toledo, Asturias, and Daanbantayan Campuses, along with Consolacion and Compostela Extension Campuses, all ready to showcase their skills, determination, and competitive spirit in the pursuit of championship titles.

Meanwhile, delegates from the remaining participating campuses are also accommodated at CTU Danao Campus as part of the billeting arrangements for the event.

More than a competition, the Anggara Unity Cup serves as a platform for fostering camaraderie, strengthening campus unity, and promoting sportsmanship among CTU athletes. It also forms part of the university’s preparation for the upcoming Regional State Colleges and Universities Athletic Association (SCUAA) Meet this November at Bohol Island State University in Bohol.

As the games unfold, participating athletes are set to demonstrate not only their athletic prowess but also the discipline, teamwork, and determination that embody the true spirit of sports./Cherry K. Luminario and Meljane P. Payot

posts.title: FSG Student Dialogue strengthens student representation, responsive governance at CTU
posts.excerpt: Student leaders from the various campuses of Cebu Technological University (CTU) convened this morning at the Main Campus for the Federation of Student Governments (FSG) Student Dialogue with the Vice President…
posts.contentHtml:
Student leaders from the various campuses of Cebu Technological University (CTU) convened this morning at the Main Campus for the Federation of Student Governments (FSG) Student Dialogue with the Vice President for Student Affairs Dr. Romeo P. Montecillo.

The dialogue served as a platform for FSG officers and campus presidents to raise concerns, share campus-specific issues, and discuss matters affecting the student body directly with the Office of the VPSA.

Discussions focused on recommendations and proposed actions to enhance student welfare, services, and engagement across the University.

The meeting was headed by Dr. Montecillo, VPSA and FSG Adviser, alongside Dr. Johnry P. Dayupay, FSG Adviser from the Moalboal Campus, with the participation of the Federation’s executive officers and board members.

Reinforcing student-centered governance, today’s dialogue enabled meaningful engagement between University leaders and student representatives, fostering collaboration and responsive action on student concerns.

posts.title: RAISE Program Phase 2 drives CTU’s efforts in innovation, IP protection, and technology transfer
posts.excerpt: Cebu Technological University (CTU) continues to support research, protect intellectual property, and promote the commercialization of innovative technologies through a coordination meeting for Phase 2 of its I…
posts.contentHtml:
Cebu Technological University (CTU) continues to support research, protect intellectual property, and promote the commercialization of innovative technologies through a coordination meeting for Phase 2 of its Intellectual Property and Technology Business Management (IPTBM) and Agri-Aqua Technology Business Incubator (ATBI) projects under the RAISE Program.

Held on October 28, the meeting gathered representatives from the RAISE Program, CTU administrators, and project implementers to review the accomplishments of Phase 1, discuss the plans and targets for Phase 2, and ensure that the projects remain aligned with the university’s research and development priorities.

Discussions centered on strengthening intellectual property protection, enhancing technology transfer mechanisms, and translating research outputs into practical and marketable innovations. Particular emphasis was placed on fostering technology-based enterprises in the agriculture and aquatic sectors.

On behalf of OIC University President Dr. Jonita V. Literatus, Vice President for Research Administration and Finance Dr. Ramel C. Genobiagon represented the CTU administration, along with Vice President for Research and Development Dr. Pet Roey L. Pascual.

Through this initiative, CTU continues to recognize the importance of collaboration, institutional support, and shared efforts in turning research into meaningful innovations.

The university remains committed to advancing the goals of the RAISE Program and creating more opportunities for technology development and commercialization in Phase 2./Zandel Kim S. Ebro, BSFIL Intern

posts.title: Women 3.0 highlights women’s health and breast cancer awareness
posts.excerpt: Promoting greater awareness of women’s health, Cebu Technological University (CTU)-Main Campus, through its College of Arts and Sciences, concluded its Women 3.0: Narratives of Change project on November 3. Imp…
posts.contentHtml:
Promoting greater awareness of women’s health, Cebu Technological University (CTU)-Main Campus, through its College of Arts and Sciences, concluded its Women 3.0: Narratives of Change project on November 3. Implemented in partnership with Barangay Ermita, Cebu City, and CVCCO Multipurpose Cooperative, the initiative highlighted menopause management, breast health, and the importance of preventive healthcare.

The event featured a breast health check-up and wellness talk by Dr. Maybeline Estroso, a menopause specialist from Cebu South Medical Center, who discussed menopause self-management and the importance of regular health monitoring and preventive care.

During the program, Project Leader Dr. Reah G. Fabrica posed a thought-provoking question: “Where do menopausal women belong?”


“Through Women 3.0, the answer became clear: menopausal women belong in spaces where they are valued, supported, and empowered to thrive,” she said.

Dr. Fabrica also acknowledged the project team for sharing their expertise and demonstrating dedication and commitment throughout the initiative.

Representing the project’s 25 beneficiaries, Esterlita Aparis shared how the initiative had positively influenced their lives.

Beyond gaining valuable knowledge about menopause, she said, the participants found a supportive community where they felt seen, understood, and encouraged to prioritize their health and well-being.

The program also gathered representatives from partner agencies and stakeholder groups, reflecting a shared commitment to advancing women’s welfare.

Among those present were Maricar T. Bontuyan, Mayor’s Representative; Rosalima A. Cimagala, Cebu City GAD Focal Person; Dr. Rannie Corazon P. Gravador of the Department of Health-CVCHD; Ashley D. Conde of the DSWD Region VII Women Welfare Program; and Jonah V. Ceso V, MPA, DILG Cebu Director.

One significant outcome was the commitment expressed by government partners to support the expansion of CTU’s Menopause Project.

The initiative aims to extend its reach to more communities by bringing evidence-based health services and advocacy closer to menopausal women in the barangays./Cheryl Rose Alojacin, BSFIL Intern
posts.author: Junas Flores

posts.title: ACCREDITATION UPDATE | AACCUP Survey Visit reinforces quality standards across 3 CTU Campuses
posts.excerpt: In line with its continuing pursuit of academic quality and institutional excellence, Cebu Technological University’s Argao, Barili, and Consolacion campuses participated in the AACCUP accreditation survey visi…
posts.contentHtml:
In line with its continuing pursuit of academic quality and institutional excellence, Cebu Technological University’s Argao, Barili, and Consolacion campuses participated in the AACCUP accreditation survey visit held from November 2 to 6.

The AACCUP survey team was led by Dr. Analyn M. Gamit of Nueva Ecija University of Science and Technology, Overall Coordinator for Argao Campus; Dr. Sherrilyn G. Quintos of Bataan Peninsula State University, Overall Coordinator for Barili Campus; Dr. Jovita E. Villanueva of Bulacan State University and Assoc Prof. Joji Ann M. Fama of Don Mariano Marcos Memorial State University, overall coordinators for Consolacion Campus.

Argao Campus underwent Level I accreditation for its Bachelor of Secondary Education major in Mathematics and Bachelor of Arts in Literature programs.

Consolacion Campus, under Level I accreditation, presented its Bachelor of Science in Information Technology, BS in Hospitality Management, BS in Business Administration major in Financial Management, BSED with majors in English, Filipino, and Mathematics, Bachelor of Elementary Education, and BA in Political Science programs for evaluation.

Meanwhile, Barili Campus presented for Level I accreditation its BS in Food Technology, BS in Agribusiness, and BSED with major in English programs, while its BS in Development Communication and BSED major in Science were assessed.

The survey visit was facilitated by the Quality Assurance Office under Dr. Meralei J. Lawas, with support from OIC President Dr. Jonita V. Literatus, represented by University Dean of Instruction Dr. Ariel L. Ramos.

Supporting the accreditation process were Campus QA Chairs Dr. Melanie R. Albarracin, represented by Dean of Instruction Dr. Fitzgerald C. Kintanar (Argao), Engr. Yvonne P. Elizalde (Barili), and Asst. Prof. Arvin B. Salera (Consolacion), and campus directors Dr. Eingilbert C. Benolirao, Dr. Sarah Jane A. Colina, and Dr. Romeo C. Lepiten, represented by Assistant Campus Director Dr. George A. Albarracin.

The evaluation covered key quality assurance areas, including student support services, faculty, curriculum and instruction, research, extension and community development, VMGO, library services, facilities, laboratories, and administration.

As a key quality assurance mechanism, the evaluation guided efforts to strengthen academic quality, institutional governance, and service delivery across CTU campuses.

posts.title: LOOK | CTU Main conducts 4th Quarter National Simultaneous Earthquake Drill
posts.excerpt: Cebu Technological University–Main Campus conducted its 4th Quarter National Simultaneous Earthquake Drill (NSED) earlier today, November 5, 2026, involving students, faculty members, and university personnel.…
posts.contentHtml:
Cebu Technological University–Main Campus conducted its 4th Quarter National Simultaneous Earthquake Drill (NSED) earlier today, November 5, 2026, involving students, faculty members, and university personnel.

Participants practiced the “Duck, Cover, and Hold” technique and followed established evacuation procedures to reinforce earthquake preparedness and emergency response.

The drill was led by the university’s Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (DRRMO), Quick Response Team (QRT), and Reserve Officers’ Training Corps (ROTC), in collaboration with the Campus Medical Team and Civil Security Unit (CSU).

In accordance with Campus Memorandum No. CD-J27-364, s. 2026, the activity aimed to strengthen the university’s disaster resilience and ensure an organized evacuation during emergencies.

posts.title: QS World University Rankings 2027:Asia
posts.excerpt: Cebu Technological University (CTU) has been named as one of Asia’s top universities,according to the 2027 edition of the QS World University Rankings: Asia. The rankings, released yesterday by global higher ed…
posts.contentHtml:
Cebu Technological University (CTU) has been named as one of Asia’s top universities,according to the 2027 edition of the QS World University Rankings: Asia.

The rankings, released yesterday by global higher education analyst Quacquarelli Symonds, saw CTU place #1201-1300 in Asia, 190 in Southeast Asia and #20 in the Philippines.

This year’s ranking is the largest ever, featuring more than 1700 universities across 26 higher education systems,including 45 in Philippines.

posts.title: CTU marks 1,000th Scopus-indexed publication milestone
posts.excerpt: Recognized for its sustained research productivity, Cebu Technological University (CTU) received the 1000th Scopus Research Award from Global Health Focus (GHF) University Excellence after recording its 1,000th…
posts.contentHtml:
Recognized for its sustained research productivity, Cebu Technological University (CTU) received the 1000th Scopus Research Award from Global Health Focus (GHF) University Excellence after recording its 1,000th Scopus-indexed publication on November 3, 2026.

The award recognizes CTU’s sustained commitment to research excellence and continuous scientific publication. Based on its Scopus profile, the University has produced 1,000 documents contributed by 1,178 authors across various disciplines.

Further reinforcing the University’s research distinction, this milestone attests to the sustained efforts of its faculty, researchers, and academic community to produce impactful research and foster a culture of innovation across disciplines.

posts.title: ACCREDITATION UPDATE | Four campuses complete AACCUP Accreditation Survey Visit
posts.excerpt: As part of its continuing quality assurance efforts, Cebu Technological University’s Daanbantayan, Barili, Dumanjug Extension, and Carmen campuses underwent the accreditation survey visit of the Accrediting Age…
posts.contentHtml:
As part of its continuing quality assurance efforts, Cebu Technological University’s Daanbantayan, Barili, Dumanjug Extension, and Carmen campuses underwent the accreditation survey visit of the Accrediting Agency of Chartered Colleges and Universities in the Philippines (AACCUP) from October 26 to 30.

The AACCUP survey team was led by Dr. Liza L. Quimson of Pangasinan State University (PSU), Overall Coordinator for the Carmen, Barili, and Daanbantayan campuses, alongside Dr. Jennifer G. Fronda, Overall Coordinator for Dumanjug Ext. campus.

Programs assessed included:

Daanbantayan Campus

Level II

Bachelor of Industrial Technology major in Computer Technology

Barili Campus

Level II (Revisit Areas IV and VI)

Bachelor of Science in Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering

Dumanjug Extension Campus

Level II (Revisit All Areas)

BS in Mechanical Engineering

BS in Electrical Engineering

Bachelor of Elementary Education

Level I (Revisit All Areas)

BS in Civil Engineering

Carmen Campus

Level I

BS in Marine Engineering

The five-day survey visit was facilitated by the Quality Assurance Office under University Director Dr. Meralei J. Lawas, with support from Campus QA Chairs Engr. Yvonne P. Elizalde (Barili), Dr. Bonifacio M. Amper Jr. (Carmen), Dr. Lovella Cristianne A. Gulle (Daanbantayan), and Dr. Samuel C. Villa Jr. (Dumanjug Ext.). 

Supporting the accreditation process were University Dean of Instruction Dr. Ariel L. Ramos, and campus directors Dr. Romeo C. Lepiten (Barili); Dr. Anthony S. Ilano (Carmen); Dr. Rowena P. Dato-on (Daanbantayan); and Dr. Rolito T. Imperial (Dumanjug Ext.).

During the survey visit, evaluators assessed key areas including student support services, faculty qualifications, curriculum and instruction, research, extension and community development, CTU’s Vision, Mission, Goals, and Objectives (VMGO), library services, physical plant and facilities, laboratories, and administration.

The weeklong evaluation served as a vital mechanism for institutional reflection and enhancement, guiding CTU in further strengthening its academic programs, governance systems, and service delivery across its campuses.

posts.title: Second-Year students undergo development workshop on adjustment and resilience
posts.excerpt: Cebu Technological University-Main Campus, through the Guidance Services Center-Day Program, conducted the two-day student development workshop, “From Freshman Spark to Sophomore Stride: Adjusting, Adapting, an…
posts.contentHtml:
Cebu Technological University-Main Campus, through the Guidance Services Center-Day Program, conducted the two-day student development workshop, “From Freshman Spark to Sophomore Stride: Adjusting, Adapting, and Thriving in Year Two,” on October 20-21.

The workshop aimed to equip second-year students with the knowledge, skills, and resilience needed to navigate the academic, social, emotional, and personal challenges of their sophomore year, fostering a smoother transition and continued success in university life.

In her welcome remarks, Guidance Services Specialist Dr. Josephine A. Villa stressed the value of independence and personal growth in college.

“College life is about being independent and then training yourself to be a good worker or business person someday,” she said.

Dr. Villa also emphasized that “adjusting is an ongoing process,” encouraging participants to remain patient with themselves as they adapt to new academic demands and changing social environments.

The two-day event convened second-year students from the Bachelor of Secondary Education (BSEd), Bachelor of Elementary Education (BEEd), Bachelor of Technical-Vocational Teacher Education (BTVTEd), Bachelor of Technology and Livelihood Education (BTLEd), and Bachelor of Early Childhood Education (BECEd) programs.

Dr. Catherine Ross D. Degula led the lecture, “Navigating the Second-Year Transition,” highlighting the sophomore year as the “forgotten year,” when students often face heavier academic and personal challenges.

She emphasized the importance of adjusting to new environments, adapting to responsibilities, and thriving through resilience and growth despite difficulties.

The workshop was organized in response to survey findings showing that many second-year students face academic challenges and uncertainty about their chosen programs. Guidance interns Mary Bhel O. Guillemer and Hannah Margreth V. Martinez presented the Academic Adjustment Scale results and facilitated reflection activities that encouraged students to share coping strategies for sophomore life.

Through this initiative, CTU upholds its dedication to student well-being by equipping future educators with the resilience, self-awareness, and skills needed to overcome academic challenges and thrive throughout their university journey./Mary Cris Butal Custodio & Cheryl Rose Alojacin, BSFIL Interns

posts.title: Malaysia’s top-tier Multimedia University has CTU academic talking global economy
posts.excerpt: Asst. Prof. Anne Jere Bajarias served as a resource speaker on transnational entrepreneurship for the webinar series at the International Virtual Mobility Programme 2026, hosted by ally Multimedia University, o…
posts.contentHtml:
Asst. Prof. Anne Jere Bajarias served as a resource speaker on transnational entrepreneurship for the webinar series at the International Virtual Mobility Programme 2026, hosted by ally Multimedia University, one of Malaysia’s top-tier HEIs.

Delivering the session titled “Understanding the Business World: From Ideas to Enterprises in a Changing Global Economy,” the College of Management and Entrepreneurship academic brought together students from CTU and MMU for an exchange of knowledge.

She examined how business ideas can evolve into viable enterprises in a changing global economy, emphasizing the importance of innovation, entrepreneurship, adaptability, and strategic thinking in responding to emerging opportunities and challenges.

The virtual mobility, running from October 19 to November 1, features a rich encounter of academic and cultural sessions covering legal systems, university life, food heritage, sports and the law, DNA evidence, business, festivals, artificial intelligence, folklore, traditional songs and dances, and education.

The collaboration etched a chapter in the recently formalized partnership (initiated by Carmen’s Dr. Purity Mata, who is also taking a role as one of the three CTU lecturers).

posts.title: Sewing, Souvenir-making Training opens livelihood pathways for DSWD Home for Girls beneficiaries
posts.excerpt: Beneficiaries of the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) Home for Girls in Labangon, Cebu City are now better equipped with practical livelihood skills following a five-day sewing and souvenir-m…
posts.contentHtml:
Beneficiaries of the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) Home for Girls in Labangon, Cebu City are now better equipped with practical livelihood skills following a five-day sewing and souvenir-making training conducted by the College of Technology through its Bachelor of Industrial Technology (BIT) in Garments Technology Program.

Held from September 14-18, the “Sewing Skills Training for DSWD Beneficiaries (Year 4): Crafting Souvenirs with Application of Fabric Manipulation and Ornaments” provided hands-on training in sewing, fabric manipulation, ornament application, and souvenir-making, equipping participants with skills for potential livelihood opportunities.

The initiative stemmed from a partnership formalized through a Memorandum of Agreement signed in August 2026 by Ms. Jennifer Abastillas, Center Head of the DSWD Home for Girls, and DSWD Regional Director Shalaine S. Lucero.

Opening the program, Ms. Jennifer Abastillas and Dr. Maria Esther F. Medalla, Associate Dean of COT and project leader, encouraged participants to maximize the training as a pathway to personal and livelihood development.

Project Leader Mr. Joseph D. Arquillano led the training, overseeing the orientation, assessment, and workshop activities while guiding participants in hands-on sewing, fabric manipulation, and souvenir-making exercises.

The training also benefited from the support and technical assistance of BIT Garments Technology interns, supervised by Ms. Hanna Grace Zulita.

Also supporting the initiative were the COT’s Machine Shop and Mechatronics Programs, represented by Dr. Cecilio Baga, Dr. Miguelito Laug-Laug, and Mr. Marniel Albinto, who serviced and repaired the center’s sewing machines to sustain future livelihood and income-generating activities.

On September 18, the training culminated in a graduation and product showcase, where participants presented their finished souvenirs and expressed gratitude for the skills and knowledge gained to support future livelihood opportunities.

The initiative reinforces CTU’s role in empowering communities through skills development and partnerships that foster self-reliance and sustainable livelihoods among DSWD beneficiaries.
